author: Booger Boner
title: The low down
content:
I saw a review talking about how higher level players look down on smaller non cash spending players.
There’s a couple holes in this statement.
Most players get into an alliance where the bigger players get them more rewards and help them get through big builds.
They are needed for participation in alliance challenges and if they are helpful with tasks are a big part of the team.
My experience has been as I grow and learn the game my interaction with bigger players has led to my success getting to more powerful levels.
Everyone deals with the pay aspect and the game has developed better participation challenges that really help new players get through new levels faster. This includes better hero frags that were not available to us in the past.
It is a long form alliance game so it does take some time to make the biggest levels but if you enjoy this kind of game it’s pretty fun to play.
Last I would say when you first start out keep looking for an alliance that chats and is inclusive.
My first alliances didn’t know what they were doing and I reached to alliances that were better. Even the ones that attacked me.
Good luck

author: Zyomag
title: Read before playing
content:
After playing this game for almost 6 months this is my conclusion. 
To make it short this game is designed for someone who is  either willing to spend a lot of money or a LOT of time on it. 
If you limit your daily, or only play a couple of times a week, or less you will end up losing most of your resources, and trying to constantly rebuild your sanctuary. The game is designed to pray on weaker sanctuaries and there is always someone stronger. There are events that happen a few times a month that encourage players to attack what you may have been building for months. Since they are usually stronger there’s no way to retaliate. If you’re not checking in every hour you may miss some of these events or possibility to grow and end up being set back. I see 10-20 sanctuaries (daily) abandoned because the players have given up. Because of this toxic and hostile environment I give only 2 stars. If you play a few hours every day it can be somewhat interesting (but not captivating) because of the connection with other players. That’s why I didn’t leave 1 star.

author: igetchestpains
title: scam likely
content:
i would challenge any developer of this game to justify the absurd pricing found within. 
the social aspect is (can be) enjoyable, but that community is built by the players, not the game. as far as the actual gameplay goes, it’s just a never ending cycle of collect and spend, collect and spend. there are frequent events throughout the week, most of which are hamstrung by varying levels of poor design; but even these are repetitive and usually reskinned or renamed variations of the same thing. on top of this they have inadvertently created a cannibalistic server ecosystem where the oldest “states” become stagnant due to literal month long build/research times on single upgrades and no possible progression in pvp events. so the strongest players continually migrate to new servers that seem to pop up every week. younger states are dominated by big spenders and overpowered bullies, which causes players to leave in frustration or migrate to other states which then causes a collapse there and the cycle continues. one avenue the game pushes relentlessly to dangle a balance of power in front of you is - you guessed it - spend an insane amount of money. every day.
the only redeeming quality is managing to find a decent group of folks to play with. also the name of this game is awful. and “puzzles” is a stretch.
